title: Placement - where should the course start?
instructions: Five questions. Ask ALL of them before revealing any answer. Do not hint. Do not say which answer is right. Lettered options, one letter per reply.

scoring.method: Add the level_points of every question answered correctly.
scoring.note: If the learner says they already know where they want to start, honour it and skip this. Record the path as self-selected.

questions.prompt: A large language model is best described as:
options: A program that looks up the correct answer in a big table
A function fitted to a lot of text that turns a prompt into a probability distribution over what could come next
A hand-written set of rules for each question type
A database of customer tickets and their answers
questions.explain: An LLM learns statistical structure from text and produces probabilities over continuations. That is why it can write a sentence nobody wrote, and why it can also be confidently wrong - the output is a distribution, not a lookup.

questions.prompt: A model returns probabilities for four possible answers. What must be true about those four numbers?
options: They sum to 1
They are all different
They are all above 0.5
They are all integers
questions.explain: Probabilities from a single distribution always sum to 1 - that is what makes them probabilities rather than scores. They can be equal, they can all be below 0.5, and they are never integers.

questions.prompt: Softmax converts a list of raw scores (logits) into:
options: A probability distribution that sums to 1
A list of whole numbers
The gradient of the loss
A list of text tokens
questions.explain: Softmax exponentiates the scores and normalises them, so the result is positive and sums to 1. Gradients come from the chain rule on the loss; tokens come from the tokenizer.

questions.prompt: You raise the temperature above 1 when sampling. What happens to the distribution?
options: It becomes sharper - the top option takes more of the probability mass
It becomes flatter - the mass spreads across more options
The options get re-sorted alphabetically
The smallest probability is rounded to zero
questions.explain: Temperature above 1 divides the logits, shrinking the gaps between them, so the softmax is flatter. Below 1 it sharpens. The ranking never changes either way - only the mass does.

questions.prompt: You want to compare two model providers on your own support tickets. What do you need before any comparison means anything?
options: Your tickets with the correct answer attached to each one
A larger GPU
A bigger model than both providers offer
The vendor's published benchmark table
questions.explain: Without outcome labels there is nothing to be right or wrong against - you can measure agreement between providers, but not accuracy. A vendor benchmark measures the vendor's workload, which is not yours.
